lessons.title: Früher war alles anders: telling about a change and a happy moment
lessons.goal: Tell a change story with früher, a turning point and inzwischen, use verändern and sich verändern, and describe your happiest moment.

grammar.topic: Telling a change story: früher – dann – inzwischen
grammar.point: A change story has three steps: früher + Präteritum (war, hatte, wohnte), a turning point with dann or auf einmal, and inzwischen or mittlerweile + Präsens or Perfekt. Verändern needs someone who changes something (Der Umzug hat mein Leben verändert); sich verändern happens by itself (Berlin hat sich verändert).
grammar.oneLine: Früher wohnte ich in Wien, inzwischen wohne ich in Berlin.

mistake.why: The time word takes position 1, so the verb stays in position 2 and the subject follows.

terms.meaning: to change something / to change by itself
turning point: the moment when something changes in a life or a story
by now, in the meantime

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Ich wohne in Berlin' to 'Früher wohnte ich in Wien'
cards.body: For the radio show „Wendepunkte“ Mira and Leon want stories about change: how life was before, what changed it, and how it is today. You can already say früher, heute and the past of war, hatte and many verbs. Today you put them into a story and learn the verb for change: verändern.
steps: You already know: Heute wohne ich in Berlin. Früher war ich in Wien. Heute with the Präsens, früher with the one-word past.
New today: Berlin hat sich verändert. Der Umzug hat mein Leben verändert. Plus inzwischen, mittlerweile and auf einmal to move a story forward.
By the end you can: tell a short change story with früher, a turning point and inzwischen, and describe your happiest moment.

examples.de: Heute wohne ich in Berlin.
examples.en: Today I live in Berlin.
examples.why: You know this: heute with the Präsens.

examples.de: Früher war ich in Wien.
examples.en: I was in Vienna earlier.
examples.why: You know this too: früher with war.

examples.de: Berlin hat sich verändert.
examples.en: Berlin has changed.
examples.why: New today: the verb for change.

cards.more: Think of your phone's photo album. Three photos from three years: one from before, one from the day something happened, one from now. A change story is exactly this album in words. Früher is the old photo, written in the one-word past. The turning point is the middle photo, still in the past. Inzwischen or heute is the newest photo, in the present. German gives you small words that act like the dates under the photos.

cards.title: verändern or sich verändern?
cards.body: Verändern needs somebody or something that changes something: Der Umzug hat mein Leben verändert. Sich verändern happens by itself, so sich is the object: Berlin hat sich verändert. Both use haben in the Perfekt. The noun is die Veränderung. Sich entwickeln means to develop, and the noun is die Entwicklung.
cards.lead: The key verb of today comes first. These examples show the two patterns side by side, so you can see when the change has a cause and when it simply happens.

examples.de: Der Umzug hat mein Leben verändert.
examples.en: The move changed my life.

examples.de: Berlin hat sich verändert.
examples.en: Berlin has changed.

examples.de: Mira hat sich in Berlin gut entwickelt.
examples.en: Mira has developed well in Berlin.

examples.de: Die Veränderung war groß.
examples.en: The change was big.

deeper.text: In everyday talk people also say ändern and sich ändern, the shorter cousins: Das ändert nichts. Das Wetter hat sich geändert. Der Wandel is the formal word for big changes in society, as in der Wandel der Zeit, with the genitive you already know. In a radio show about life stories, Veränderung is the best everyday choice.

example.de: Das ändert nichts.
example.en: That changes nothing.

cards.more: Picture a wall. If you take a pot of paint and paint it red, you change the wall: that is verändern with an object, Ich habe die Wand verändert. If the sun makes the paint fade, the wall changes by itself, and sich is the little helper: Die Wand hat sich verändert. So ask yourself one question: Who does it? If somebody does it, verändern. If it just happens, sich verändern. The same helps with sich entwickeln: it grows by itself.

rows: Der Umzug hat mein Leben verändert.

cards.title: Früher, dann, inzwischen: the order of a change story
cards.body: A change story has three steps. Früher describes the old situation, in the Präteritum: war, hatte, wohnte. Then comes the turning point, with dann or auf einmal. Finally inzwischen or mittlerweile says how it is by now, in the Präsens or the Perfekt. Heute closes the story.
cards.lead: Now the order of a story. Mira's own change from Wien to Berlin shows the three steps one after the other, with the little time words in position 1.

examples.de: Früher wohnte Mira in Wien.
examples.en: Earlier Mira lived in Vienna.

examples.de: Dann zog Mira nach Berlin um.
examples.en: Then Mira moved to Berlin.

examples.de: Inzwischen hat Mira viele Freunde gefunden.
examples.en: By now Mira has found many friends.

examples.de: Heute fühlt sich Mira in Berlin wohl.
examples.en: Today Mira feels at home in Berlin.

deeper.text: Inzwischen and mittlerweile both mean by now and are nearly the same, but mittlerweile often sounds a little more surprised. Inzwischen has a second meaning: meanwhile, at the same time. Ich koche, und inzwischen rufst du Mira an. The time word stays in position 1 or after und, and the verb stays right after it.

example.de: Ich koche, und inzwischen rufst du Mira an.
example.en: I cook, and in the meantime you call Mira.

cards.more: Think of three photos in a row. Photo one has the label früher and shows the old life, in the one-word past. Photo two has the label dann or auf einmal and shows the day that changed things. Photo three has the label inzwischen and shows life now, in the present. If you say the labels aloud while you tell your story, the order is automatic. And the verb always sits in position 2, right behind the label.
steps: Start with the old situation: Früher war ich … / Früher wohnte ich …
Say what changed it: Dann zog ich um. / Auf einmal kam …
Finish with now: Inzwischen habe ich … Heute bin ich …

cards.title: The happiest moment: Augenblick and Gänsehaut
cards.body: For the radio show Mira also asks: Was war der schönste Augenblick in Ihrem Leben? You answer with the words Augenblick (moment), unvergesslich (unforgettable), Gänsehaut haben (to get goose bumps), vor Freude weinen (to cry with joy) and überwältigt sein (to be overwhelmed).
cards.lead: Now the feelings. These words let you describe a big moment, and the examples are the ones that Ben, Leon and Mira would say on the radio.

examples.de: Der schönste Augenblick war, als ich Anna kennengelernt habe.
examples.en: The most beautiful moment was when I met Anna.

examples.de: Ich hatte Gänsehaut, als die Musik anfing.
examples.en: I got goose bumps when the music started.

examples.de: Mira hat vor Freude geweint.
examples.en: Mira cried with joy.

examples.de: Das war ein unvergesslicher Augenblick.
examples.en: That was an unforgettable moment.

deeper.text: Einen Augenblick, bitte! is the polite way to ask somebody to wait a moment. Im Augenblick means at the moment, as in Im Augenblick bin ich sehr glücklich. So Augenblick is both a special moment and a short wait, and the little phrases are used every day, in shops and on the phone.

example.de: Im Augenblick bin ich sehr glücklich.
example.en: At the moment I am very happy.

cards.more: Imagine you carry a small camera in your head. Most days it stays off. But sometimes something happens, the music starts, a person walks in, a result arrives, and the camera clicks. That click is an Augenblick. The skin on your arms reacts, that is Gänsehaut. Your eyes get wet, that is vor Freude weinen. You are overwhelmed, überwältigt. Today you learn the words for the photos in your head, and you can share one of them with the radio.

cards.title: Auf einmal: one story, spoken and written
cards.body: Auf einmal and plötzlich both mean suddenly. They move the story forward at the turning point. In a spoken story the verb is in the Perfekt, in a written one in the Präteritum. Here is one scene from Leon's first day in the kitchen, told twice. The words auf einmal and plötzlich never change.
cards.lead: Here is the choice rule from today's first lesson once more, now with a turning point. The same scene appears twice so you can compare spoken and written style.

examples.de: Auf einmal ist Herr Ali gekommen.
examples.en: Spoken: Suddenly Herr Ali came.

examples.de: Auf einmal kam Herr Ali.
examples.en: Written: Suddenly Herr Ali came.

examples.de: Plötzlich hat Herr Ali gesagt: Heute kochst du!
examples.en: Spoken: Suddenly Herr Ali said: Today you cook!

examples.de: Plötzlich sagte Herr Ali: Heute kochst du!
examples.en: Written: Suddenly Herr Ali said: Today you cook!

deeper.text: Auf einmal has a second meaning: at the same time, all at once. Alle haben auf einmal gesprochen means everybody spoke at once. The meaning depends on the sentence. At the start of a sentence, with a turning point, it means suddenly. After the verb, with a group of people, it means at once. Plötzlich only ever means suddenly.

example.de: Alle haben auf einmal gesprochen.
example.en: Everybody spoke at once.

cards.more: Think of a film. A quiet scene, the music is calm, and then: cut! The light changes, the door opens, somebody walks in. Auf einmal is the cut. It marks the second photo of the story. In a voice message you say it with the Perfekt and a lively voice. In a book you write it with the Präteritum. The word itself is the same in both. Try this: say the scene aloud twice, once as a voice message, once as a book page.

rows: Auf einmal ist Herr Ali gekommen.
Er hat Leon eine Schürze gegeben.
Er hat gesagt: Heute kochst du!

cards.title: Street interview: Was hat sich in Ihrem Leben verändert?
cards.body: Mira and Leon ask six people on the campus: Was hat sich in Ihrem Leben verändert? The answers are short and spoken, so they use früher with war, hatte or the Perfekt, and inzwischen or mittlerweile for now. Read them and look for the three steps from before.
cards.lead: Now listen to the street. Six short answers, like in the Easy German videos, show the change stories of real people, in just one sentence each.

examples.de: Früher war ich sehr still, aber mittlerweile spreche ich gern vor Gruppen.
examples.en: A student: Earlier I was very quiet, but by now I like to speak in front of groups.

examples.de: Früher bin ich jeden Tag zur Arbeit gefahren, jetzt habe ich Zeit für meinen Garten.
examples.en: A pensioner: Earlier I drove to work every day, now I have time for my garden.

examples.de: Mein Leben hat sich mit dem Kind total verändert.
examples.en: A parent: My life has changed completely with the child.

examples.de: Damals konnte ich nur Hallo sagen, inzwischen spreche ich viel.
examples.en: A newcomer: Back then I could only say hello, by now I speak a lot.

examples.de: Früher habe ich nur gearbeitet, heute treffe ich oft Freunde.
examples.en: A cook: Earlier I only worked, today I often meet friends.

examples.de: Berlin hat sich sehr verändert, es gibt jetzt viele neue Cafés.
examples.en: A resident: Berlin has changed a lot, there are many new cafés now.

deeper.text: Look at the question: Was hat sich verändert? Here was is the subject, the thing that changed, so there is nothing to put into the accusative. Sich comes right after the verb. In an interview people ask with Sie: in Ihrem Leben, bei Ihnen. With friends you use dir and dein: Was hat sich in deinem Leben verändert? The pattern is exactly the same.

example.de: Was hat sich in Ihrem Leben verändert?
example.en: What has changed in your life?

cards.more: Think about the three-sentence answer that works for every person. Sentence one: how it was. Sentence two: what changed. Sentence three: how it is now. The six street answers cut it down even more, into one sentence with a comma in the middle: before, comma, now. That is the shortest version of a change story. Use it when somebody asks you quickly. Use the long version when you have time.

cards.title: Your turn: a speaking frame for the radio
cards.body: Here is a six-sentence monologue that works as a speaking frame. Sentences one and two describe the old situation. Sentence three is the turning point. Sentence four is the big moment. Sentence five says how it is by now. Sentence six is the feeling today. Change the content, keep the frame.
cards.lead: The last card is your own tool. Leon's monologue for the radio shows the six sentences in order, and you can replace one detail at a time with your own life.

examples.de: Früher war ich sehr unsicher: Ich wusste nicht, was ich werden wollte.
examples.en: Earlier I was very unsure: I did not know what I wanted to become.

examples.de: Ich hatte keinen Plan.
examples.en: I had no plan.

examples.de: Dann habe ich samstags in einer Küche geholfen.
examples.en: Then I helped in a kitchen on Saturdays.

examples.de: Auf einmal wusste ich: Kochen macht mich glücklich.
examples.en: Suddenly I knew: cooking makes me happy.

examples.de: Inzwischen koche ich jeden Samstag für viele Gäste.
examples.en: By now I cook for many guests every Saturday.

examples.de: Heute bin ich viel gelassener als früher.
examples.en: Today I am much calmer than before.

deeper.text: End your radio monologue with a question for the listeners. That is how presenters keep people engaged: Und Sie? Was hat sich bei Ihnen verändert? Notice that this is a short question without a verb in the first part, and the second part is the pattern from the street interview. Radio German is often spoken in such short, direct sentences.

example.de: Und Sie? Was hat sich bei Ihnen verändert?
example.en: And you? What has changed for you?

cards.more: Imagine a bridge with six pillars. Pillar one and two stand on the old bank: the old situation. Pillar three is in the water: the turning point. Pillar four is the highest: the big moment. Pillar five is near the new bank: by now. Pillar six is the new bank: today. If a pillar is missing, the bridge falls down. So count to six while you speak, and your story always arrives on the other side.
steps: Sentences 1 and 2: Früher war ich … Ich hatte …
Sentences 3 and 4: Dann … Auf einmal …
Sentences 5 and 6: Inzwischen … Heute …

lessons.title: Während der Sendung: während, innerhalb, außerhalb + genitive
lessons.goal: Say when something happens or where it is with während, innerhalb and außerhalb plus the genitive, and read a radio running order.

grammar.point: während (during), innerhalb (within) and außerhalb (outside of) are prepositions with the genitive: des for masculine and neuter nouns (with -s or -es), der for feminine nouns and plurals, eines or einer after a. Without an article use innerhalb von + dative. statt (instead of) also takes the genitive. In speech many people use the dative after während; in writing the genitive is standard.
grammar.oneLine: Während der Sendung ruft ein Hörer an.

mistake.wrong: Während die Sendung ruft ein Hörer an.
mistake.right: Während der Sendung ruft ein Hörer an.
mistake.why: während with a noun is a preposition and needs the genitive: der Sendung. Innerhalb eine Woche has the same problem: say innerhalb einer Woche.

terms.meaning: a preposition that is followed by the genitive: während, innerhalb, außerhalb, statt, wegen, trotz
running order: a list of what happens when in a show

cards.title: Before we start: from wegen des Regens to während der Sendung
cards.body: Mira and Leon prepare the first episode of „Wendepunkte“ (Turning Points), a show on the campus radio. A running order is full of time words: when does what happen, and inside which hour? Three small words help, and they all take the genitive, like wegen and trotz.
steps: You already know: wegen des Regens, trotz des Regens. After these words the article is des (masculine, neuter) or der (feminine, plural).
New today: während der Sendung (during the show), innerhalb einer Woche (within a week), außerhalb der Öffnungszeiten (outside opening hours).
By the end you can: put a time or place with während, innerhalb and außerhalb into the correct genitive, and read a radio running order.

examples.de: Trotz des Regens sendet Leon live.
examples.en: Despite the rain, Leon is broadcasting live.
examples.why: You know this: trotz + genitive.

examples.de: Während der Sendung ruft ein Hörer an.
examples.en: During the show a listener calls.
examples.why: New today: the same genitive, now with a time word.

cards.more: Think of the genitive as a small club with its own entry words. You met two members, wegen and trotz. Today three more join: während, innerhalb, außerhalb. The article does not change from what you know. Masculine and neuter nouns get des and -s, feminine nouns and plurals get der. The only new thing is the meaning: all three words are about time or place, so they fit perfectly into a running order for a radio show.

cards.title: während + genitive: during something
cards.body: während answers the question When? and means during. The noun after it stands in the genitive: während des Studiums, während der Sendung, während des Interviews, während der Ferien. Here während is a preposition with a noun, not a conjunction with a clause. The clause use comes later.
cards.lead: You know the genitive after wegen and trotz. This card adds the first of three time words, während, and shows its four article forms in one table.

examples.de: Während des Studiums wohnt Mira in Berlin.
examples.en: During their studies Mira lives in Berlin.

examples.de: Während der Sendung ruft ein Hörer an.
examples.en: During the show a listener calls.

examples.de: Leon kocht während der Ferien jeden Tag.
examples.en: Leon cooks every day during the holidays.

deeper.text: während tells you that two things overlap in time. It does not say how long something lasted. For the length of time German uses a plain accusative or für: Ben hat zwei Stunden geschlafen. Compare Während der Fahrt hat Ben geschlafen: it happened at some moment inside the trip, and you do not know for how long.

example.de: Während der Fahrt hat Ben geschlafen.
example.en: Ben slept during the trip.

cards.more: Picture während as a box. The noun after it is the box, and the other event happens somewhere inside. English says during and then the noun, and German does the same, only the noun must change its article. Use the same articles as after wegen: des for masculine and neuter, der for feminine and for every plural. Say it out loud twice: während des Studiums, während der Sendung.

cards.title: innerhalb and außerhalb: time and place
cards.body: innerhalb means within, außerhalb means outside of. Both work for time and for place, and both take the genitive. Time: innerhalb einer Woche, außerhalb der Arbeitszeit. Place: innerhalb der Stadt, außerhalb Berlins. A city name without an article gets an -s.
cards.lead: During is one time word. Now you meet a pair that marks the borders: what is inside a time or a space, and what is outside of it.

examples.de: Das Studio liegt innerhalb des Campus.
examples.en: The studio is inside the campus.

examples.de: Außerhalb der Öffnungszeiten ist das Studio zu.
examples.en: Outside opening hours the studio is closed.

examples.de: Innerhalb einer Stunde beginnt die Sendung.
examples.en: Within an hour the show begins.

deeper.text: When there is no article, German often uses innerhalb von with the dative instead of the bare genitive: innerhalb von zwei Tagen, innerhalb von Berlin. With a bare plural like zwei Tage the genitive would sound stiff. The same works for außerhalb von. Watch the small word von: it is easy to forget in speech.

example.de: Mira schickt den Text innerhalb von zwei Tagen.
example.en: Mira sends the text within two days.

cards.more: Think of a fence. Innerhalb is the inside of the fence, außerhalb is the outside. The fence can be time (an hour, a week, opening hours) or place (a city, a campus). Because the fence is a noun, the noun goes into the genitive. If you are unsure, ask yourself: could I say in or outside of in English? Then innerhalb or außerhalb fits, and the genitive follows.

cards.title: Build it in three steps
cards.body: The same three steps work for all three words. First the preposition, then the genitive article, then the noun. Masculine and neuter nouns take -s or -es. Feminine nouns and plurals take no ending. With ein you say eines (masculine, neuter) and einer (feminine).
cards.lead: You have seen the three words. This card gives you one routine for building any phrase with them, including the forms after ein.

examples.de: Innerhalb eines Jahres hat sich viel verändert.
examples.en: Within a year a lot has changed.

examples.de: Während einer Pause trinkt Leon Kaffee.
examples.en: During a break Leon drinks coffee.

examples.de: Innerhalb einer Woche muss Mira den Text schreiben.
examples.en: Within a week Mira has to write the text.

deeper.text: Which ending does the noun get, -s or -es? Short nouns with one syllable mostly take -es: des Jahres, des Tages. Longer nouns take -s: des Interviews, des Studiums. Nouns ending in -s, -ß or -z always take -es: des Hauses. You hear the difference, so trust your ear. A wrong choice here is a small slip that people forgive.

example.de: Während des Tages ist es im Studio ruhig.
example.en: During the day it is quiet in the studio.

cards.more: Treat the phrase like a small recipe. Ingredient one: the preposition. Ingredient two: the article, des or der, or eines or einer if you mean a. Ingredient three: the noun, with -s only if it is masculine or neuter. The sentence around it does not change at all: it simply starts with the phrase or contains it later. Cook it three times with different nouns, and it will stay in your head.
steps: 1. Choose the preposition: während, innerhalb or außerhalb.
2. Put the article in the genitive: des (m, n), der (f, pl), eines (m, n), einer (f).
3. Add -s or -es to a masculine or neuter noun, nothing to feminine nouns and plurals.

cards.title: Preposition or clause?
cards.body: A preposition with a noun is shorter than a clause. Als wir das Interview gemacht haben, war Mira nervös. Während des Interviews war Mira nervös. The same shortcut works for weil and obwohl: wegen des Regens, trotz des Regens. Use the noun version when you want a short, written style.
cards.lead: You now have a whole family of genitive prepositions. This card compares them with the clauses you already know, so you can choose the shorter way.

examples.de: Während des Interviews war Mira nervös.
examples.en: During the interview Mira was nervous.

examples.de: Wegen des Regens bleiben wir zu Hause.
examples.en: Because of the rain we stay at home.

examples.de: Trotz des Regens fahren wir ins Studio.
examples.en: Despite the rain we drive to the studio.

deeper.text: In speech many Germans say während dem Essen with the dative. You will hear it all the time, and everyone understands it. The standard in writing, in exams and in a job letter is the genitive: während des Essens. So recognise the dative in conversation, but write and say the genitive when you want to sound careful.

example.de: Während des Essens telefoniert Leon nicht.
example.en: Leon does not make phone calls during the meal.

cards.more: Two ways to say the same idea. With a clause you need a verb: Als wir das Interview gemacht haben, war Mira nervös. With a preposition you need only a noun: Während des Interviews war Mira nervös. The second one is shorter, so it fits headlines and radio plans. Keep the clause when you want to tell what exactly happened. Both are correct German, so it is a question of style.

rows: Als wir das Interview gemacht haben, war Mira nervös.
Während des Interviews war Mira nervös.
Weil es regnet, bleiben wir zu Hause.
Wegen des Regens bleiben wir zu Hause.
Obwohl es regnet, fahren wir ins Studio.
Trotz des Regens fahren wir ins Studio.

cards.title: Mira's running order
cards.body: Mira writes a running order (Ablaufplan) for the show. Each line starts with a time word, and then the verb follows in second position, and the subject comes after it. Read it like a radio producer: what happens during the music, what happens within the hour, what happens outside airtime?
cards.lead: You can build the phrases. Now you read them in a real text: Mira's plan for the first episode, where every line starts with a time word.

examples.de: Während der Musik telefonieren wir mit dem Gast.
examples.en: During the music we phone the guest.

examples.de: Innerhalb einer Stunde spielen wir fünf Lieder.
examples.en: Within an hour we play five songs.

examples.de: Außerhalb der Sendezeit nehmen wir die Interviews auf.
examples.en: Outside airtime we record the interviews.

deeper.text: Starting a sentence with the time phrase puts the verb in position 2 and the subject right behind it. That is why the plan reads Während der Musik telefonieren wir. If you start with the subject, the phrase moves inside and the meaning stays the same: Wir telefonieren während der Musik mit dem Gast. Both are fine. The plan simply prefers the first version, because the time word is the news.

example.de: Wir telefonieren während der Musik mit dem Gast.
example.en: We phone the guest during the music.

cards.more: A running order is a to-do list in time. Each line answers one question: when? So each line starts with a time phrase, and the rest is a normal sentence. The verb always comes second, even after a long phrase like außerhalb der Sendezeit. Try reading the plan aloud like a producer. Tick off each line as you say it. The lines are short, and the pattern repeats, so the genitive will soon feel natural.

cards.title: statt + genitive: instead of
cards.body: statt (or anstatt) means instead of and also takes the genitive: statt eines Interviews eine Umfrage, statt der Musik ein Gespräch. Without an article it simply stands before the noun: statt Musik ein Gespräch. That is all for today, one short card.
cards.lead: The last word of the family is a small extra. statt does not talk about time, but it takes the same genitive you just practised.

examples.de: Statt eines Interviews macht Mira eine Umfrage.
examples.en: Instead of an interview Mira does a survey.

examples.de: Statt der Musik gibt es ein Gespräch.
examples.en: Instead of the music there is a conversation.

examples.de: Wir machen heute statt Musik ein Gespräch.
examples.en: Today we do a conversation instead of music.

deeper.text: statt and anstatt mean exactly the same. anstatt sounds a little more formal and is more common in writing. In speech you may hear statt dem Auto, with the dative, just like während dem Essen. In writing choose the genitive: anstatt des Autos. Careful: this card is only about statt with a noun. A clause with statt comes later in the course.

example.de: Anstatt des Autos nehmen wir den Bus.
example.en: Instead of the car we take the bus.

cards.more: Statt is like a swap. One thing goes out, another comes in. The thing that goes out stands in the genitive after statt, and the thing that comes in stands in its normal case, usually the accusative or nominative. Statt eines Interviews eine Umfrage: the interview goes out, the survey comes in. If a sentence says what you do instead, you have the whole swap in a single line.

lessons.title: Seit dem Umzug, bis zum Ende: time prepositions with the dative
lessons.goal: Place events in time with the dative prepositions seit, vor, nach, ab, bei, zwischen, bis zu and von … an, using the short forms beim, vom, zum and zur.

grammar.point: seit, vor, nach, ab, bei, zwischen, bis zu and von … an are followed by the dative. bei + a noun made from a verb means while doing something (beim Essen). zwischen needs two points. bis zu means until; bis alone is used with days and clock times. bei dem, von dem, zu dem and zu der become beim, vom, zum and zur.
grammar.oneLine: Seit dem Umzug wohne ich in Berlin.

mistake.wrong: Seit ein Jahr wohne ich hier.
mistake.right: Seit einem Jahr wohne ich hier.
mistake.why: seit takes the dative: einem for masculine and neuter nouns. With a long form like bei dem Essen the sentence is not wrong, only stiff; beim Essen is the normal form.

terms.meaning: a preposition that is always followed by the dative: seit, vor, nach, ab, bei, zwischen, bis zu, von … an
two words melted into one: bei dem = beim, von dem = vom, zu dem = zum, zu der = zur

cards.title: Before we start: from seit einem Jahr to bis zur Rente
cards.body: A radio show tells life stories, and life stories are full of time: since when, until when, between which events? You already own four small time words. Today you add four more, and all of them take the dative, like the words you know. The new ones are bei, zwischen, bis zu and von … an.
steps: You already know: seit drei Tagen, vor einem Jahr, nach der Arbeit, ab Montag. All four are followed by the dative.
New today: beim Kochen (while cooking), zwischen dem Studium und dem ersten Job, bis zur Rente, vom ersten Tag an.
By the end you can: place events in time with eight dative words, including the short forms beim, vom, zum and zur.

examples.de: Seit einem Jahr wohnt Leon in Berlin.
examples.en: Leon has lived in Berlin for a year.
examples.why: You know this: seit + dative, with the present tense.

examples.de: Vom ersten Tag an kocht Leon gern.
examples.en: From the first day on Leon likes cooking.
examples.why: New today: von … an, with vom = von dem.

cards.more: Think of the dative time words as a timeline with stops. Seit, vor, nach and ab you know. The new ones fill the gaps: bei is a moment while something happens, zwischen is the gap between two points, bis zu is the finish line, and von … an is the starting gun with no end. Nothing about the dative changes: dem for masculine and neuter, der for feminine, den plus -n for plural.

cards.title: seit, vor, nach, ab: the words you know
cards.body: Four dative words you know. seit means since or for and goes with the present: seit dem Umzug. vor means ago or before: vor einem Jahr. nach means after: nach der Schule. ab means from … on: ab nächster Woche. Learn them again with life events.
cards.lead: Before the new words, a short check of the four old ones, now with life events like moving, school and a wedding instead of everyday plans.

examples.de: Seit dem Umzug wohnt Mira in Berlin.
examples.en: Since the move Mira has lived in Berlin.

examples.de: Nach der Schule hat Herr Ali eine Lehre als Koch gemacht.
examples.en: After school Herr Ali did an apprenticeship as a cook.

examples.de: Ab nächster Woche sendet das Campusradio jeden Mittwoch.
examples.en: From next week the campus radio broadcasts every Wednesday.

deeper.text: seit and vor both look at the past, but they do different jobs. seit starts in the past and is still true now, so you use the present: Ich wohne seit einem Jahr hier. vor names a point that is over and uses a past tense: Ich bin vor einem Jahr umgezogen. A mistake with these two is the most common one at B1, so check which one you mean.

example.de: Vor einem Jahr ist Mira umgezogen.
example.en: A year ago Mira moved.

cards.more: Draw a line with a dot for now. Seit starts left of the dot and runs up to it: you are still in it. Vor is a dot left of now, and the story stops there. Nach is the point after something, ab is the point from which something begins. The dative tells you nothing about which one to choose. Only the meaning does: still going on, long ago, afterwards, or from now on.

cards.title: bei + dative: while doing something
cards.body: bei + dative means during or while doing something. It often goes with a verb used as a noun: beim Essen, beim Kochen, beim Aufnehmen. Such nouns are neuter and capitalised. bei dem becomes beim. You also say bei der Arbeit when the noun is already a noun.
cards.lead: The old words say when something starts or stops. bei describes the moment while an action is going on, and it works with verbs turned into nouns.

examples.de: Beim Essen spricht Leon über die Sendung.
examples.en: During the meal Leon talks about the show.

examples.de: Mira hört beim Kochen gern Radio.
examples.en: Mira likes listening to the radio while cooking.

examples.de: Beim Aufnehmen darf niemand sprechen.
examples.en: Nobody may talk while recording.

deeper.text: bei has a second meaning you know from A1: at someone's place, bei Anna, bei meiner Tante. Do not mix the two. If a person follows, it is about a place. If a verb-noun follows, it is about time. Both take the dative, so the grammar does not help you here. Only the meaning does.

example.de: Bei Frau Weber trinken wir beim Lernen Tee.
example.en: At Frau Weber's place we drink tea while studying.

cards.more: Take a verb, put das in front, and the verb becomes a noun: essen, das Essen. Now beim gives you a short way to say while eating. In English you say while plus the ing-form, and German says bei plus the noun. The noun is always neuter, so the article is always dem, which melts into beim. Try it with kochen, lernen and schlafen, and you can make a dozen new phrases.

cards.title: zwischen and bis zu: gaps and finish lines
cards.body: zwischen + dative means between two points: zwischen dem Studium und dem ersten Job, zwischen 8 und 9 Uhr. bis zu + dative means until: bis zum Abitur, bis zur Rente. With a weekday or a clock time bis stands alone, without zu and without an article: bis Montag, bis 18 Uhr.
cards.lead: Now two words for the edges of a time span: zwischen marks both ends, bis zu marks only the end, the finish line.

examples.de: Zwischen der Lehre und dem Umzug nach Berlin arbeitete Herr Ali in Basel.
examples.en: Between the apprenticeship and the move to Berlin Herr Ali worked in Basel.

examples.de: Die Sendung läuft zwischen 18 und 19 Uhr.
examples.en: The show runs between 6 and 7 pm.

examples.de: Bis zum Abitur wohnte Mira bei den Eltern.
examples.en: Until her school leaving exam Mira lived with her parents.

deeper.text: bis zu also stands before numbers and then means up to: bis zu fünfzig Hörer, bis zu zehn Minuten. After zu a number needs no case ending at all. Be careful with the weekday or clock version: bis Montag means until Monday, and bis 18 Uhr means until 6 pm. There is never an article and never a zu in these two.

example.de: Bis zu fünfzig Hörer rufen jede Woche an.
example.en: Up to fifty listeners call every week.

cards.more: Think of a ruler. Zwischen needs two marks on it, so you always say two things: zwischen dem Studium und dem Job. Bis zu needs only the right mark, the end. Both look at the dative: dem for masculine and neuter, der for feminine. If you forget the second part with zwischen, the sentence feels unfinished, just like the English between needs an and. Say it with und, and you are safe.

rows: zwischen dem Studium und dem ersten Job
bis zum Abitur, bis zur Rente

cards.title: von … an, ab and the short forms
cards.body: von … an + dative means from … on: vom ersten Tag an, von Montag an. ab + dative says nearly the same: ab dem ersten Tag. The little words melt with the article: bei dem, beim, von dem, vom, zu dem, zum, zu der, zur. In speech and writing you use the short form almost always.
cards.lead: You have all eight words. This card ties up two loose ends: the pair von … an, which comes in two pieces, and the short forms that you must use every day.

examples.de: Vom ersten Tag an arbeitet Mira im Campusradio.
examples.en: From the first day on Mira works at the campus radio.

examples.de: Ab dem ersten Tag hatte Leon Spaß.
examples.en: From the first day on Leon had fun.

examples.de: Von Montag an sendet das Radio jeden Tag.
examples.en: From Monday on the radio broadcasts every day.

deeper.text: von … an sounds a little stronger than ab: it stresses that something changed at this moment and stays that way. Typical are von heute an and von jetzt an, which have no article at all. You can also say ab heute. When von is followed by a bis, you get a span: von 18 bis 19 Uhr, from six until seven.

example.de: Von heute an macht Leon jeden Morgen Sport.
example.en: From today on Leon does sport every morning.

cards.more: Treat von … an like a sandwich: von is the first slice, an is the last slice, and the time word is the filling between them. Ab is a single slice, which is why people say it more often. For the melting words, think of dem as glue: bei, von and zu stick to dem and become beim, vom and zum. Only zu stays alone with der and becomes zur, written as one word.

cards.title: Dative or genitive? Two ways to say it
cards.body: Some time ideas have two forms. The genitive version is more formal and written: während des Essens, innerhalb eines Jahres. The dative version is shorter and more spoken: beim Essen, in einem Jahr. Both are correct German. Use the first when you write and the second when you talk.
cards.lead: You now know the genitive words from the last lesson and the dative words from this one. Here you see how they overlap in meaning.

examples.de: Beim Essen telefoniert Leon nicht.
examples.en: Leon does not make phone calls while eating.

examples.de: Während des Essens telefoniert Leon nicht.
examples.en: Leon does not make phone calls during the meal.

examples.de: In einem Jahr ist die Aufnahme fertig.
examples.en: In a year the recording is finished.

deeper.text: The overlap is not complete. In einem Jahr means a year from now, at the end of the year. Innerhalb eines Jahres means at any time before the year has gone. Also, seit and während are never twins: während overlaps with something, seit starts in the past and runs up to now. Choose by meaning first, style second.

example.de: Innerhalb eines Jahres hat Anna drei Bilder gemalt.
example.en: Within a year Anna painted three pictures.

cards.more: Make yourself a tiny map. Genitive: während, innerhalb, außerhalb, statt, wegen, trotz. Dative: seit, vor, nach, ab, bei, zwischen, bis zu, von … an. Memorise the genitive group as a family of six, since the others all follow the dative without any rule. If you are in doubt, the dative is a safe default for the time words in this lesson. In writing, choose the genitive where you can.

cards.title: Herr Ali's story as a radio teaser
cards.body: A radio teaser introduces a guest in a few lines. Mira writes one for Herr Ali. Each line starts with a time phrase, and the verb follows in position 2. She uses only facts: Herr Ali lived in Zürich as a child, did an apprenticeship, worked in Basel and has cooked in Berlin for over 20 years.
cards.lead: Everything comes together here: eight dative time words in one short text, the radio teaser for the guest in the next lesson.

examples.de: Bis zu seinem 16. Geburtstag lebte Herr Ali in Zürich.
examples.en: Until his 16th birthday Herr Ali lived in Zürich.

examples.de: Seit über 20 Jahren kocht Herr Ali in Berlin.
examples.en: For over 20 years Herr Ali has cooked in Berlin.

examples.de: Vom ersten Tag an war „Zum Löwen“ voll.
examples.en: From the first day on „Zum Löwen“ was full.

deeper.text: Notice the tenses in the teaser. The story of the past is in the Präteritum: lebte, arbeitete. What is still true today is in the present: Seit über 20 Jahren kocht er in Berlin. That is the same rule as for seit in the first card. A radio host often mixes both, because the host tells a story and also says what is true now.

example.de: Zwischen 1996 und 2001 arbeitete Herr Ali in Basel.
example.en: Between 1996 and 2001 Herr Ali worked in Basel.

cards.more: A teaser is a trailer for a person. It works in three beats: the childhood, the turning point, and today. Each beat starts with a different time word, so the lines do not sound the same. Childhood: bis zu. Turning point: zwischen or nach. Today: seit. Count the beats in Mira's teaser. If you want to write your own teaser, copy this pattern and swap the facts.

lessons.title: Herzlich willkommen bei „Wendepunkte“!: making a radio programme
lessons.goal: Understand and make a short radio programme with a welcome, an interview with Sie and a caller, using the Präteritum for the prepared text, the Perfekt for speaking and the time prepositions, and pronounce consonant clusters.

grammar.topic: using Präteritum, Perfekt and time prepositions in a radio programme
grammar.point: No new grammar. A prepared moderation uses the Präteritum (Herr Ali wuchs in Zürich auf). Live questions and answers use the Perfekt (Ich bin mit 25 nach Berlin gekommen) and war, hatte and the modal verbs in the Präteritum. The time prepositions from lessons 7 and 8 structure the text. Thanks takes für + accusative.

mistake.wrong: Ich habe mit 25 nach Berlin gekommen.
mistake.right: Ich bin mit 25 nach Berlin gekommen.
mistake.why: kommen is a verb of movement and forms the Perfekt with sein, not haben.

terms.meaning: the spoken text of the host that welcomes listeners and connects the parts of a show
several consonants in a row in one word, like Herbst

cards.title: Before we start: from listening to the radio to making it
cards.body: Today there is no new grammar. Mira and Leon prepare the first episode of „Wendepunkte“ with Herr Ali as the guest. You use what you already know: the Präteritum for a prepared text, the Perfekt for speaking, and the time words from the last two lessons. New are the radio phrases and a few hard sounds.
steps: You already know: interview questions with Sie, like Wann sind Sie nach Berlin gekommen? You also know the Perfekt for speaking and the Präteritum for stories.
New today: radio phrases like Herzlich willkommen bei … and Bleiben Sie dran!, the order of a show, and consonant clusters like Herbst.
By the end you can: follow the structure of a radio programme, welcome a guest, react to a caller and pronounce Herbst and Angst.

examples.de: Wann sind Sie nach Berlin gekommen?
examples.en: When did you come to Berlin?
examples.why: You know this: a polite interview question in the Perfekt.

examples.de: Herzlich willkommen bei „Wendepunkte“!
examples.en: A warm welcome to „Wendepunkte“!
examples.why: New today: the fixed greeting at the start of a show.

cards.more: A radio show is a recipe, and today you learn the order of the steps. The grammar is already in your pocket. The prepared welcome is written German read aloud, so it uses the Präteritum: Herr Ali wuchs in Zürich auf. The live questions and answers are normal speech, so they use the Perfekt: Ich bin mit 25 nach Berlin gekommen. Only a handful of fixed phrases are new, and you can learn them as whole pieces.

cards.title: The order of a radio programme
cards.body: A radio programme has a clear order. First the greeting, then the topic, then the guest. After the interview comes music or a transition. Then listeners phone in, and at the end the host says goodbye. Fixed phrases help at every step: Herzlich willkommen bei …, Heute geht es um …, Bei mir im Studio ist …, Bleiben Sie dran!
cards.lead: You know what a show needs. This card puts the parts in order and gives you the typical sentence for each one.

examples.de: Heute geht es um Veränderungen.
examples.en: Today it is about changes.

examples.de: Bei mir im Studio ist Herr Ali.
examples.en: In the studio with me is Herr Ali.

examples.de: Bleiben Sie dran!
examples.en: Stay tuned!

deeper.text: A news-style show says Sie to the audience: Bleiben Sie dran! A youth or campus show often says ihr: Bleibt dran! Both are friendly. The host picks one form and keeps it for the whole show, because switching would sound odd. For the guest the host always says Sie in a first interview, unless they know each other well and agree on du.

example.de: Bleibt dran, wir sind gleich zurück!
example.en: Stay tuned, we will be right back!

cards.more: Think of a radio show as a train with seven stops. The host is the driver, and the listeners ride along. At each stop there is a short announcement, and you already know what it says: welcome, topic, guest, interview, music, phone calls, goodbye. If you hear the announcement, you know where the train is, even if you do not understand every word. Learn the seven stops, and you can follow any show.
steps: 1. Begrüßung: Herzlich willkommen bei …
2. Thema: Heute geht es um …
3. Gast vorstellen: Bei mir im Studio ist …
4. Interview
5. Musik oder Überleitung: Nach der Musik …
6. Hörer am Telefon
7. Verabschiedung: Das war … für heute.

cards.title: The interview with Herr Ali
cards.body: Here is the first show. Mira introduces the guest in the Präteritum, because the text is prepared: Herr Ali wuchs in Zürich auf. In the live interview she says Sie to Herr Ali and speaks in the Perfekt. Only war, hatte and modal verbs stay in the Präteritum when people speak.
cards.lead: The order is clear. Now you read a real interview from the first show, where you see the prepared welcome and the live talk side by side.

examples.de: Herr Ali wuchs in Zürich auf und machte mit 16 eine Lehre als Koch.
examples.en: Herr Ali grew up in Zürich and did an apprenticeship as a cook at 16.

examples.de: Wann sind Sie nach Berlin gekommen?
examples.en: When did you come to Berlin?

examples.de: Ich hatte kaum Geld, und ich konnte nicht gut Deutsch.
examples.en: I had hardly any money, and I could not speak German well.

deeper.text: Look at the interview with the tenses in mind. Mira's welcome says wuchs auf and machte, the written style. Herr Ali answers with ist gekommen, the Perfekt, and with hatte and konnte, the Präteritum of the small verbs. Even in one show you hear both tenses, and nobody notices a break. It just feels like a natural mix of a prepared text and live talk.

example.de: Zwei Jahre nach dem Umzug haben wir das Restaurant aufgemacht.
example.en: Two years after the move we opened the restaurant.

cards.more: If you want to understand the interview, listen for two kinds of sentences. The questions from Mira are short and usually start with a question word or with the verb. The answers from Herr Ali are longer and tell a little story. Each answer has a time word, like vor über 20 Jahren or vom ersten Tag an. Spot these time words and you can follow the story, even when you miss a few of the other words.

rows: Herr Ali wuchs in Zürich auf und machte mit 16 eine Lehre als Koch.
Herr Ali, willkommen! Wann sind Sie nach Berlin gekommen?
Ich bin vor über 20 Jahren gekommen, mit 25.
Schwer. Ich hatte kaum Geld, und ich konnte nicht gut Deutsch.
Wann haben Sie das Restaurant aufgemacht?
Zwei Jahre nach dem Umzug. Vom ersten Tag an war es voll.
Was hat sich seit damals verändert?
Alles und nichts. Ich koche noch jeden Tag, aber inzwischen habe ich ein großes Team.
Vielen Dank! Nach der Musik sprechen wir über Ihr Rezept.

cards.title: Listeners call in
cards.body: After the music the listeners call in. A caller tells a short story about their own turning point. The host reacts with a short sentence before the next question: Das klingt spannend! At the end of the call the host says thank you: Vielen Dank für Ihren Anruf!
cards.lead: The interview is over. Now the phone rings, and you see how Mira answers a caller in two or three short sentences.

examples.de: Mein Wendepunkt war der Umzug nach Hamburg.
examples.en: My turning point was the move to Hamburg.

examples.de: Das klingt spannend!
examples.en: That sounds exciting!

examples.de: Vielen Dank für Ihren Anruf!
examples.en: Thank you very much for your call!

deeper.text: Thanking uses für plus the accusative: Danke für den Tipp, Vielen Dank für Ihren Anruf, Danke für deine Geschichte. After für the feminine and plural forms look like the nominative, and only the masculine changes: der Anruf becomes den Anruf. That is the accusative rule you know. The same pattern works for every thank-you in daily life.

example.de: Vielen Dank für Ihre Geschichte!
example.en: Thank you very much for your story!

cards.more: A host reacts like a good friend. First comes a small reaction, which shows interest. Then maybe one question that goes deeper. At the end comes the thanks. Three little steps, and the caller feels heard. In German these reactions are short and fixed, so you can learn them like vocabulary: Das klingt spannend, Wie interessant, Das verstehe ich gut. Say one of them in your next conversation.

rows: Mein Wendepunkt war der Umzug nach Hamburg.
Das klingt spannend! Warum sind Sie umgezogen?
Beim Kochen hatte ich die Idee für meine Firma.
Wie interessant! Seit wann gibt es die Firma?
Seit dem Umzug bin ich viel glücklicher.
Das freut mich. Vielen Dank für Ihren Anruf!

cards.title: Pronunciation: many consonants in a row
cards.body: German has words with three, four or five consonants in a row: Herbst, Angst, du schreibst, selbstständig, Strumpf, Obst, Wendepunkt. The trick is to speak slowly and say every consonant. Do not push a vowel in between: it is Herbst, not Her-e-bst. Say the cluster as one quick block.
cards.lead: You have the radio phrases. Now you practise the sounds that scare many learners: words where consonants stand in a long row.

examples.de: Im Herbst schreibst du selbstständig deinen ersten Beitrag.
examples.en: In autumn you write your first contribution on your own.

examples.de: Ich habe Angst vor dem Mikrofon.
examples.en: I am afraid of the microphone.

examples.de: Zum Frühstück esse ich Obst.
examples.en: For breakfast I eat fruit.

deeper.text: The letter b at the end of a syllable sounds like p. So du schreibst sounds like schreipst, and Obst sounds like Opst. This is called final devoicing, and it also works for d (Rad sounds like Rat) and g (Tag sounds like Tak). You still write b, d and g, so spell the base word to know which letter you need.

example.de: Du schreibst einen Text für die Sendung.
example.en: You write a text for the show.

cards.more: Think of a drum roll. Each consonant is one quick tap, and there is no pause between the taps. Start slowly with Herbst: h, e, r, b, s, t. Then say it again at normal speed. For Wendepunkt split it into two words, Wende and Punkt. First say each part alone, then glue them together. The glue is the small d–p–k stretch. Never add an uh sound in the middle.

rows: say rbst quickly, no vowel after r
ng like in Ring, then st
lips together for m, then p, then f
say Wende and Punkt, then join

cards.title: Write a 60-second moderation
cards.body: A short welcome has four parts: the greeting, the topic, the guest and the hook for after the music. You can fill a frame with your own facts. Use the Präteritum for the guest's past, because the text is prepared and written. Then read it aloud slowly, and say each cluster clearly.
cards.lead: You have heard a whole show. Now you build the first minute yourself: a frame with four slots that you fill with your own words.

examples.de: Herzlich willkommen bei „Wendepunkte“!
examples.en: A warm welcome to „Wendepunkte“!

examples.de: Er kam vor über 20 Jahren nach Berlin.
examples.en: He came to Berlin over 20 years ago.

examples.de: Nach der Musik sprechen wir über seine Küche.
examples.en: After the music we talk about his kitchen.

deeper.text: Why the Präteritum in the frame? A moderation is prepared and read aloud, so it is like a written text spoken aloud: Er kam, er machte. The improvised questions to the guest are normal speech, with the Perfekt: Wann haben Sie angefangen? Both tenses live in the same show, and now you know why. The rule is the same as in lesson 4 of this chapter.

example.de: Er machte mit 16 eine Lehre als Koch.
example.en: At 16 he did an apprenticeship as a cook.

cards.more: A frame is a sentence with holes. Instead of staring at a blank page you fill four holes: who, what, which guest, what comes next. Take Mira's frame and change the facts: another guest, another topic. The grammar stays the same, since the verbs are in the Präteritum and the time phrases are the same. Keep your text short, because a minute on the radio is shorter than you think.

rows: Bei mir im Studio ist … Er kam …
Bei mir im Studio ist Herr Ali. Er kam vor über 20 Jahren nach Berlin.
Nach der Musik … Bleiben Sie dran!
Nach der Musik sprechen wir über seine Küche. Bleiben Sie dran!

cards.title: Listening tip: understand the radio
cards.body: Radio is fast, and you cannot go back. Three tricks help. First, listen for the topic in the first 20 seconds, because the host always says it early. Second, listen for names. Third, listen for numbers, such as years and times. If you catch these three, you understand the main story even when many words are new.
cards.lead: You can make a moderation. The last card helps you with the other side: understanding a real show when the host speaks quickly.

examples.de: Das Campusradio begann 2012 mit drei Studierenden.
examples.en: The campus radio began in 2012 with three students.

examples.de: Die Sendung läuft von 18 bis 19 Uhr.
examples.en: The show runs from 6 to 7 pm.

examples.de: Heute sprechen wir mit drei Gästen.
examples.en: Today we talk with three guests.

deeper.text: Years sound different from what you may expect. You say 2012 as zweitausendzwölf, but 1998 as neunzehnhundertachtundneunzig. From 2000 on German uses the long form, before 2000 it uses hundreds, like English nineteen ninety-eight. You often hear years inside a short sentence, so practise saying them out loud with a time phrase before it.

example.de: Herr Ali ist seit zweitausendeins in Berlin.
example.en: Herr Ali has been in Berlin since 2001.

cards.more: Imagine a net with three holes: topic, names, numbers. While you listen, you try to catch one thing in each hole. If a word is lost, do not stop. The net still holds the other things. After the first listening you know what the show is about and who speaks. After the second listening you add the numbers. This is exactly how people listen to a radio in a language they do not know perfectly.
steps: 1. In the first 20 seconds: find the topic (Heute geht es um …).
2. Listen for names: the host, the guest, places.
3. Listen for numbers: years, times, ages.

lessons.goal: Describe an object (shape, material, use) and an event (Ben's first training) in detail, and explain why boxing clubs are more than sport.

grammar.topic: Using adjective endings and the Präteritum to describe (new forms: schlug, gewann, verlor)
grammar.point: No new grammar today. You describe an object with adjective endings (ein roter Boxhandschuh, eine schwere Tasche) and aus + material without an article (aus Leder). You report an event in the Präteritum. Three sport verbs are new in the past: schlagen – schlug, gewinnen – gewann, verlieren – verlor.

cards.title: Before we start: from 'ein roter Ball' to 'ein roter Boxhandschuh'
cards.body: Ben has a new hobby: he boxes in a Boxverein in Berlin. Leon is sceptical: Ist das nicht gefährlich? Today you describe a thing and an event in detail. You need no new grammar. Adjective endings and the Präteritum do the work. Only three past forms are new: schlug, gewann, verlor.
steps: You already know: adjective endings (ein roter Ball, eine kleine Tasche) and the Präteritum for written stories (Herr Ali kam mit dem Zug nach Berlin).
New today: the words of boxing, four steps to describe an object, and schlagen – schlug, gewinnen – gewann, verlieren – verlor.
By the end you can: describe a boxing glove, report Ben's first training and say what you think about boxing for young people.

examples.en: Herr Ali came to Berlin by train.
examples.why: You know this: an irregular Präteritum form in a written story.

examples.de: Ben gewann seinen ersten Kampf.
examples.en: Ben won his first fight.
examples.why: New today: the past of gewinnen, in the same frame.

cards.more: Picture the WG kitchen on a Tuesday evening. Ben comes home late with a big sports bag and red cheeks. Leon looks up from his pasta and asks what happened. Ben has just had his first boxing training. Two things happen in this lesson. First you look closely at an object, the glove in Ben's bag. Then you follow the evening itself, from the warm-up to the end. Every sentence uses grammar you already own; only the boxing words and three past forms are new.

cards.title: Boxing words: der Ring, der Kampf, der Boxhandschuh
cards.lead: First the words of the sport. Ben uses them all the time, so learn them before we describe his glove and his training.
cards.body: The place is der Boxverein, with a Ring in the middle of the hall. You wear Boxhandschuhe, and the person in front of you is your Gegner. A Kampf has several rounds. The verbs boxen and kämpfen are regular: er boxte, sie kämpfte. A man who boxes is ein Boxer, a woman eine Boxerin.

examples.de: Ben boxt seit Oktober in einem Boxverein.
examples.en: Ben has been boxing in a boxing club since October.

examples.de: Im Ring kämpfen zwei Gegner.
examples.en: Two opponents fight in the ring.

examples.de: Der Kampf dauert drei Runden.
examples.en: The fight lasts three rounds.

deeper.text: boxen is the verb, das Boxen is the sport. Every infinitive can become a neuter noun with a capital letter: das Boxen, das Laufen, das Kochen. With bei the noun form is very common: beim Boxen means while boxing. So Beim Boxen braucht man Disziplin is a natural sentence, and you can build the same with beim Kochen or beim Laufen.

example.de: Beim Boxen braucht man Disziplin.
example.en: When boxing you need discipline.

cards.more: Walk into the club with Ben. You open a heavy door and come into a big hall. In the middle stands the Ring, with ropes on four sides. On the wall hang dozens of red and black Boxhandschuhe. Two people are in the ring: each one is the Gegner of the other. A bell rings, and a Kampf starts; after three minutes the round ends. Now say each thing you saw aloud with its article: der Ring, der Boxhandschuh, der Gegner, der Kampf.

cards.title: More than sport: Respekt, Disziplin, Fairness
cards.lead: Now you know the words of the ring. This card shows why many boxing clubs are about much more than hitting: values and rules.
cards.body: Many Boxvereine in Germany are more than a sports club. They often run projects for young people and teach Respekt, Disziplin and Fairness. Many people say the training gives them Selbstvertrauen. Ben's trainer has two clear rules. Im Ring kämpft man fair. Außerhalb des Rings gibt es keine Gewalt.
steps: Regel 1: Im Ring kämpft man fair.
Regel 2: Außerhalb des Rings gibt es keine Gewalt.
Respekt vor dem Gegner: vor und nach dem Kampf gibt man sich die Hand.
Disziplin: pünktlich zum Training kommen und gut zuhören.

examples.de: Im Ring kämpft man fair.
examples.en: In the ring you fight fairly.

examples.de: Außerhalb des Rings gibt es keine Gewalt.
examples.en: Outside the ring there is no violence.

examples.de: Das Training gibt Ben Selbstvertrauen.
examples.en: The training gives Ben self-confidence.

deeper.text: Respekt takes the preposition vor plus the dative: Respekt vor dem Gegner, Respekt vor dem Trainer. English says respect for, so learners often write für by mistake. In the same way Angst vor and Achtung vor use vor. The opposite of fair is unfair, and in sport German also uses the English phrase das Fair Play.

example.de: Ben hat Respekt vor seinem Gegner.
example.en: Ben has respect for his opponent.

cards.more: Look at the words like an English speaker. Respekt, Disziplin and Fairness look almost like English, so you can read them at once. Only the stress moves: in Disziplin it is on the last syllable, -plin. Selbstvertrauen is a word you can build: selbst means self, Vertrauen means trust. Self plus trust gives self-confidence. Gewalt is the hard one, because it looks like nothing in English. Think of the trainer's second rule: outside the ring, keine Gewalt, no violence at all.

cards.title: Describe an object in four steps
cards.lead: Ben shows Leon his new glove. To describe it well, you answer four questions in a fixed order, with the adjective endings you already know.
cards.body: Answer four questions in order. Was ist es? Wie sieht es aus? (colour, shape, size) Woraus ist es? Use aus + material with no article: aus Leder, aus Metall. Wofür braucht man es? Then use adjective endings: ein roter Boxhandschuh, eine schwere Tasche, ein weiches Handtuch.
steps: Was ist es? Das ist ein Boxhandschuh.
Wie sieht es aus? Er ist rot und ziemlich groß.
Woraus ist es? Er ist aus Leder und innen weich.
Wofür braucht man es? Man trägt ihn beim Training und beim Kampf.

examples.de: Das ist ein roter Boxhandschuh aus Leder.
examples.en: This is a red boxing glove made of leather.

examples.de: Er ist schwer, aber innen weich.
examples.en: It is heavy, but soft inside.

examples.de: Man trägt ihn beim Training.
examples.en: You wear it at training.

deeper.text: German often packs the material into one compound noun, with the material first: der Lederhandschuh (a glove of leather), der Holztisch, die Metallflasche. The last part gives the article. So you can say ein Handschuh aus Leder or ein Lederhandschuh, and both are correct. After an adjective in front of the noun, the material stays behind it: ein roter Handschuh aus Leder.

example.de: Der Pokal ist aus Metall.
example.en: The trophy is made of metal.

cards.more: Play a guessing game in the WG. Ben describes something from his bag without saying its name, and the others guess. He starts with the look: Es ist rot und ziemlich groß. Then the material: Es ist aus Leder. Then the use: Man trägt es an der Hand, beim Training. Anna laughs and says: Ein Boxhandschuh! Try it yourself with a thing on your desk. Colour and shape first, material second, use last. If the others guess quickly, your description was good.

cards.title: Ben's first training in the Präteritum: schlug, gewann, verlor
cards.lead: Now from the glove to the evening. Ben writes about his first training for the club website, so the written past is needed, with three new sport verbs.
cards.body: A written report uses the Präteritum. Three sport verbs are new in the past: schlagen – schlug, gewinnen – gewann, verlieren – verlor. Like kam and ging, ich and er/sie have no ending: ich schlug, er gewann. With wir and sie add -en: wir verloren. Ben's report: Das Training begann um sieben. Zuerst liefen wir.

examples.de: Das Training begann um sieben Uhr.
examples.en: The training started at seven o'clock.

examples.de: Dann schlug ich zum ersten Mal auf einen Sandsack.
examples.en: Then I hit a punching bag for the first time.

examples.de: Unser Verein gewann drei Kämpfe und verlor nur einen.
examples.en: Our club won three fights and lost only one.

deeper.text: schlagen also has an umlaut in the present: du schlägst, er schlägt, like fahren – du fährst. And it means more than to hit. In sport it often means to beat someone: Deutschland schlug Spanien means Germany beat Spain. With a clock it means to strike: Die Uhr schlägt sieben. So read the context before you translate it.

example.de: Der Trainer sagt: Du schlägst zu fest.
example.en: The trainer says: You hit too hard.

cards.more: Hook each new form onto a verb you already know. schlagen goes from a to u, just like fahren – fuhr: schlagen – schlug. gewinnen goes from i to a, just like beginnen – begann: gewinnen – gewann, with the same double n. verlieren goes from ie to o, like ziehen – zog: verlieren – verlor. Say the pairs aloud in threes: fuhr, schlug; begann, gewann; zog, verlor. Three old friends carry three new forms, so there is almost nothing new to learn.

cards.title: At home in the WG: Ben tells it in the Perfekt
cards.lead: Ben wrote his report in the Präteritum. At home he speaks, so the same evening comes out in the Perfekt, and Leon has some sceptical questions.
cards.body: When Ben tells Leon about the evening, he speaks, so he uses the Perfekt: Wir sind gelaufen, ich habe geschlagen. Only war, hatte, the modals and es gab stay in the Präteritum in speech. Leon is sceptical. Ben answers with reasons.
steps: Leon: Und, wie war's?
Ben: Super, aber anstrengend! Wir sind zuerst zehn Minuten gelaufen.
Leon: Und dann? Hast du gegen jemanden gekämpft?
Ben: Nein, noch nicht. Ich habe nur auf einen Sandsack geschlagen.
Leon: Ist das nicht gefährlich?
Ben: Nein, der Trainer ist sehr streng. Wir mussten die Regeln lernen.

examples.de: Wir sind zuerst zehn Minuten gelaufen.
examples.en: First we ran for ten minutes.

examples.de: Ich habe nur auf einen Sandsack geschlagen.
examples.en: I only hit a punching bag.

examples.de: Wir mussten die Regeln lernen.
examples.en: We had to learn the rules.

deeper.text: Wie war's? is short for Wie war es? and is the most common way to ask about an event. Another everyday question uses laufen in a new sense: Wie lief das Training? or Wie ist es gelaufen? Here laufen does not mean to run. It means to go, as in How did it go? The answer can be: Es lief gut or Es ist super gelaufen.

example.de: Und, wie ist das Training gelaufen?
example.en: So, how did the training go?

cards.more: Think of two places. At Ben's desk the text goes on the club website: Zuerst liefen wir, dann schlug ich. That is the written past. At the kitchen table he talks to Leon, face to face: Wir sind gelaufen, ich habe geschlagen. Same evening, same facts, different clothes. One exception helps you: war, hatte, the modal verbs and es gab sound natural in both places. So Ben says Es war super and Wir mussten die Regeln lernen even when he speaks.

cards.title: Your opinion: Ist Boxen gut für junge Leute?
cards.lead: Leon thinks boxing is dangerous, Ben thinks it helps. This card gives you the frame to weigh both sides and then say what you think.
cards.body: Give both sides with einerseits … andererseits, then your own view. After einerseits and andererseits in position 1 the verb comes next: Einerseits kann man sich verletzen. Andererseits lernt man Disziplin. End with Meiner Meinung nach … or Ich finde, dass … and the verb at the end.
steps: Einerseits … (one side)
Andererseits … (the other side)
Meiner Meinung nach … / Ich finde, dass … (your view)

examples.de: Einerseits kann man sich beim Boxen verletzen.
examples.en: On the one hand, you can get hurt when boxing.

examples.de: Andererseits lernen junge Leute Respekt und Disziplin.
examples.en: On the other hand, young people learn respect and discipline.

examples.de: Ich finde, dass Boxen gut ist, wenn man fair kämpft.
examples.en: I think that boxing is good if you fight fairly.

deeper.text: Auf der einen Seite … auf der anderen Seite means the same as einerseits … andererseits and is very common in speech. Both work like a time word in position 1, so the verb comes next. Andererseits can also stand after a comma in the same sentence: Boxen ist hart, andererseits macht es Spaß. The second half then still has the verb right after andererseits.

example.de: Auf der einen Seite ist Boxen hart, auf der anderen Seite macht es Spaß.
example.en: On the one hand boxing is hard, on the other hand it is fun.

cards.more: Picture old kitchen scales with two plates. On the left plate Leon puts his worry: Einerseits kann man sich verletzen. On the right plate Ben puts his reasons: Andererseits lernt man Respekt, Disziplin und Fairness, und man bekommt Selbstvertrauen. Which side is heavier? That is your opinion, and it comes last: Meiner Meinung nach … A good B1 answer always fills both plates first. Examiners like it when you show the other side before you decide, even if you disagree with it.
